cards.text: Elisha is a prophet in Israel, and he meets with a group called the sons of the prophets. One day they come to him with a problem about the place where they all meet.

cards.question: What's the problem with the place where the sons of the prophets meet with Elisha?

answers.text: It's too far from the river

cards.text: Their plan: head down to the Jordan, each one gets a log, and they build themselves a place to live there. A group project where EVERYBODY brings something? Friend, I have never seen that work in my life.

cards.question: Elisha tells the sons of the prophets to go ahead with their plan to build by the Jordan.
Before they head out, one of the sons of the prophets asks Elisha for one more thing. What is it?

cards.text: “I will come,” Elisha says, and down to the Jordan they go to start cutting trees. A prophet on the job site is the boss showing up on moving day in WORK GLOVES.
Everybody's chopping. Then one man swings at a tree, and the iron axe head comes right off the handle.

cards.question: The sons of the prophets are cutting trees right by the Jordan. Where does that flying axe head end up?
The man cries out to Elisha about the lost iron axe head. What makes losing it even worse?

cards.text: Borrowed. That's borrowing your buddy's car and calling him from the side of the road like, “Sooo… about your car.” Then Elisha, the man of God, asks the man one question.

cards.question: The man just lost a borrowed axe head in the Jordan. What's the one question Elisha asks him?

answers.text: Who did you borrow it from
How did it slip off the handle

cards.text: The man shows Elisha the spot. Me? I'd have dived in face-first and sunk straight to the bottom, gold base and all.

cards.question: Elisha doesn't go into the water after the axe head. He cuts a ___ and throws it right where it fell.
Elisha throws the stick in right where the iron axe head went down. What happens next?

cards.text: IRON. FLOATING. A chunk of iron sitting on top of the Jordan like nobody ever told it it's supposed to sink.

cards.question: Elisha lifts the floating axe head out of the water himself and hands it back to the man.

cards.text: “Lift it out,” Elisha says, and the man reaches out his hand and takes it. Friend, that is the happiest “I dropped it in the river” story I have ever heard.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 6 of the 9 choice cards (cards 2, 5, 8, 9, 11 and 14). True or false appears twice and fill in the blank once, so multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The joke compares the plan to a 'group project where EVERYBODY brings something.' Most adults first picture a school assignment when they hear that, which is the kind of setting the audience rule keeps out.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids. Work, bosses and bills are fine.

findings.problem: The joke mixes two pictures. It puts a modern 'job site' into the Bible setting and then compares that to 'the boss showing up on moving day.' 'In WORK GLOVES' also suggests Elisha does the labor, but the text only says he went with them while they cut trees (2 Kings 6:4).

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The question calls it 'that flying axe head.' The text says only that the iron axe head fell into the water (2 Kings 6:5). The exaggeration is in a choice card's question, not in one of Papa Dorin's jokes.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'branch of thorns' is close in meaning to the right answer 'stick,' since a stick cut from a tree is a branch. A baker could argue it's right. It's also three words long, longer than the blank allows and longer than 'stick' and 'rope.'

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: 'branch of thorns' runs three words against one-word answers. That breaks the 1 to 2 word blank limit and makes the answers uneven in length.

rule.text: Fill in the blank: the question has a blank for 1 or 2 words.

findings.problem: This story card only reacts to the floating iron that card 14 just revealed. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move it forward. For a 7-verse passage it reads like filler.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
